# Problem 5 · Interactions I: the additive baseline

> Simulate data with **no** interaction (`set.seed(123)`, the block in the problem
> statement), then fit `lm(y ~ x1 * x2)` anyway. (a) Compare the four fitted
> coefficients with the values used to build the data, and say whether the
> `x1:x2` term is distinguishable from zero. (b) Write the full model in
> mathematical notation. (c) Differentiate the fitted mean with respect to $x_1$;
> does $x_2$ appear? (d) Evaluate the slope in $x_1$ at $x_2 = -1$ and $x_2 = +1$
> and explain why the two are not exactly equal. (e) Name the shape of the fitted
> surface and describe its contour lines.

**My work:**

```{r}
set.seed(123)
d5 <- data.frame(x1 = runif(200, -2, 2), x2 = runif(200, -2, 2))
d5$y <- 1 + 1.5*d5$x1 - 1*d5$x2 + rnorm(200, 0, 1)   # no x1*x2 term
m5 <- lm(y ~ x1 * x2, data = d5)
summary(m5)
# Your slope calculations here
```

# Problem 6 · Interactions II: a slope that moves

> Same design, now with a genuine product term (`set.seed(456)`). (a) Compare the
> coefficients with the truth (2, 1.5, −1, 2). (b) Write the model in notation.
> (c) Find the slope in $x_1$ as a formula in $x_2$ (differentiate, or factor
> $x_1$ out), and evaluate it at $x_2 = -1, 0, +1$. (d) Solve for the $x_2$ at
> which the effect of $x_1$ vanishes and compare with the generating parameters.
> (e) Explain in two sentences why "the effect of $x_1$ is 1.52" cannot be
> written for this model. (f) Name the surface and say what happened to the
> contour lines.

**My work:**

```{r}
set.seed(456)
d6 <- data.frame(x1 = runif(200, -2, 2), x2 = runif(200, -2, 2))
d6$y <- 2 + 1.5*d6$x1 - 1*d6$x2 + 2*d6$x1*d6$x2 + rnorm(200, 0, 1)
m6 <- lm(y ~ x1 * x2, data = d6)
summary(m6)
# Your slope formula and its three evaluations here
```

# Problem 7 · Interactions III: link scale vs response scale

> Binary response with a product term on the logit scale (`set.seed(789)`).
> (a) Report the four coefficients and name the scale they are on. (b) Write the
> model with its link function. (c) Write the log-odds slope in $x_1$ and
> evaluate it at $x_2 = \pm 1$. (d) Refit **without** the interaction
> (`m7add`), then use $\partial p/\partial x_1 = p(1-p)\,\beta_1$ at $x_1 = 0$
> for $x_2 = -1$ and $x_2 = +1$; report both and their ratio. (e) Explain in
> three or four sentences why the effect of $x_1$ on the probability depends on
> $x_2$ in a model with no interaction term, naming both scales.

**My work:**

```{r}
set.seed(789)
d7 <- data.frame(x1 = runif(200, -2, 2), x2 = runif(200, -2, 2))
eta <- -1 + 1.2*d7$x1 - 0.8*d7$x2 + 1.5*d7$x1*d7$x2
d7$ybin <- rbinom(200, 1, plogis(eta))
m7 <- glm(ybin ~ x1 * x2, data = d7, family = binomial)
summary(m7)
m7add <- glm(ybin ~ x1 + x2, data = d7, family = binomial)   # additive on the log-odds scale
coef(m7add)
# Your marginal-effect calculations here
```

**Answer / biological interpretation:**
